title: Past, Present and Progressive Tense
keyIdea: The tense of a verb shows when something happens. The past tense tells what is done: most verbs add -ed (jump → jumped), and some change instead (run → ran, go → went). The present tense tells about now. To show an action going on, use a helper verb and an -ing word: is or are + -ing means it is going on now (she is drumming); was or were + -ing means it was going on in the past (he was shouting). In a piece of writing, pick a tense and keep to it.

kid: A verb is a doing word. The tense of a verb tells when. Past tense tells what is done. Present tense tells about now.
Lots of verbs add ed to show the past. Today I jump. Yesterday I jumped. The end can sound like t, but we still write ed.
Some verbs are odd ones. They do not add ed. Run turns into ran. Go turns into went. See turns into saw.

To show it is still going on, add ing and a helper word. Sam is running. That is now. Sam was running. That was in the past. Use is or was for one. Use are or were for more than one. When you write a story, pick past or present. Then keep all the verbs the same.
adult: This is the Year 2 grammar objective in the English National Curriculum (2014): correct choice and consistent use of present tense and past tense throughout writing, and the progressive form of verbs in the present and past tense to mark actions in progress (for example, she is drumming, he was shouting). Year 2 children are expected to know the terms verb and tense (past, present). In the US, Common Core L.1.1e asks children to use verbs for past, present and future, L.2.1d adds frequently used irregular past forms, and L.4.1b names the progressive tenses.

English marks two tenses on the verb itself: present (walk, walks) and past (walked). The progressive is built from a form of be plus the -ing participle: am, is or are + -ing for the present progressive, was or were + -ing for the past progressive. The helper must agree with the subject (Sam is, the birds are). The simple present (I walk to school) is mostly used for habits and facts; for an action happening at this moment English normally uses the present progressive (I am walking). Will walk is often taught as the future, but the National Curriculum glossary treats it as a modal verb with no future tense, so this lesson keeps to past and present.

The regular past ending -ed is said three ways, as in jumped (t), played (d) and wanted (id), but it is always spelled -ed. The Year 1 and Year 2 spelling rules add two changes: if the root ends in e, add only d (bake, baked), and after a short vowel and one consonant, double the consonant (hop, hopped). Hoped is a different word, the past of hope. Irregular verbs change their form instead: ran, went, saw, sat, ate.

Common mistakes: adding -ed to irregular verbs (runned, goed), which is a normal sign that the child has learned the rule and is now applying it too widely; spelling the ending by sound (jumpt); a helper that does not agree (the boys was playing); and tense drift, where a story told in the past slips into the present halfway (We went to the park. We play on the swings.). In the lab your child drags sentences onto a timeline from Yesterday to Now, builds -ed past forms, chooses is, are, was or were for an -ing verb, meets the odd verbs that do not take -ed, and taps the verb that slips out of tense in three short stories.

familyTip: At tea time ask, 'What did you do today?' and listen for past verbs: played, ran, ate. Then play 'What is everyone doing now?': Dad is cooking, the cat is sleeping. If you hear runned or goed, just say the right word back: 'You ran? Wow!'

visual.caption: Done, or going on now? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drop sentences on a timeline, spell -ed past words, pick is, are, was or were, find odd past verbs and fix the verb that slips.

practice.prompt: Which sentence tells about something that is done, in the past?
practice.hint: Look for the verb that ends in -ed. That shows the past.
practice.explain: Jumped ends in -ed, so it is the past tense: the jump is done. Is jumping is going on now.

practice.prompt: A story has {a} past verbs that end in -ed, like jumped, and {b} odd past verbs, like ran. How many past tense verbs are in the story?
practice.hint: Odd verbs like ran are past tense too, even without -ed. Count both kinds.
practice.explain: {a} -ed verbs and {b} odd past verbs make {=a+b} past tense verbs.

practice.prompt: The dogs ___ barking right now. Which helper verb fits?
practice.hint: Right now means present. The dogs are more than one.
practice.explain: It is going on now and there is more than one dog, so use are: the dogs are barking.

practice.prompt: A story in the past tense has {n} verbs. {k} of them slipped into the present, like play instead of played. How many verbs are in the past tense?
practice.hint: Take the verbs that slipped away from all the verbs.
practice.explain: {n} take away {k} is {=n-k}, so {=n-k} verbs are in the past tense. The other {k} need fixing.

pool.prompt: Which is the past tense of bake?
pool.hint: Bake already ends in e. Do you need another e?
pool.explain: Bake ends in e, so just add d: baked. The ending sounds like t but is spelled ed.

pool.prompt: What is the past tense of go?
pool.hint: Go is an odd verb. It does not take -ed.
pool.explain: Go changes to went for the past: today I go, yesterday I went. Goes is present.

pool.prompt: He ___ shouting when the bell rang. Which helper verb fits?
pool.hint: The bell rang in the past. He is just one person.
pool.explain: It was going on in the past and he is one person, so use was: he was shouting.

pool.prompt: Which sentence is going on right now?
pool.hint: Now needs am, is or are with an -ing verb.
pool.explain: Are singing is the present progressive: it is going on now. Were singing and sang are past.

pool.prompt: Find the slip: We went to the beach. We swim in the sea. Then we ate ice cream.
pool.hint: The story is in the past. Which verb is not?
pool.explain: Went and ate are past, so the story is in the past. Swim slipped into the present; it should be swam.

pool.prompt: A list has {a} verbs that take -ed, like jump, and {b} odd verbs, like run. How many verbs in the list do not take -ed?
pool.hint: Odd verbs change their form instead of taking -ed.
pool.explain: Only the {b} odd verbs do not take -ed. The other {a} verbs add -ed for the past.

pool.prompt: Tom wrote {n} sentences about yesterday. {k} of them use was + -ing, like I was reading. How many of his sentences do not use was + -ing?
pool.hint: Take the was + -ing sentences away from all of his sentences.
pool.explain: {n} take away {k} is {=n-k}, so {=n-k} sentences do not use was + -ing.

pool.prompt: Which is the past tense of hop?
pool.hint: Hop has a short o sound and ends in one consonant.
pool.explain: After a short vowel and one consonant, double it: hop, hopped. Hoped is the past of hope.
